FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A41
DOL issues a Certificate of Ownership, called the title, for most vehicles, showing the registered and legal owners, the Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) and any lender, and it should be kept somewhere safe but never in the vehicle. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A41
Every vehicle must be registered with DOL, and you need a driver license to register one unless the law exempts you, in which case you file a Vehicle Registration Driver License Exemption form. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A41
New residents have 30 days to register their vehicles, while a vehicle bought in another state should be registered in Washington right away. [A41]
Why it matters: the same thirty-day window appears for new residents' driver licenses, a common pairing on the test.
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A41
To register a vehicle you need its current title, or a replacement from the issuing state if it is lost, plus a Washington driver license for every registered owner. [A41]
Source: [A41 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A42
You receive a new registration each year when you renew your tabs, and you must sign it and keep it in the vehicle. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A42
Updating the address on your driver license does not update your vehicle address, which you change separately online in License Express or at a vehicle licensing office. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A42
When you sell, trade, gift or dispose of a vehicle you must file a Vehicle Report of Sale within 5 days and take your license plates off the vehicle. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A42
A report of sale does not transfer ownership; the owner signs and dates the title for the buyer, who must bring it to a licensing office within 15 days to avoid penalty fees. [A42]
Why it matters: learners often confuse the seller's filing window with the buyer's transfer window.
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A42
A dealership may file the report of sale for you but is not required to, so filing it yourself protects you. [A42]
Source: [A42 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A43
Plates must be displayed clean and readable on both the front and rear of a Washington-registered vehicle, and a plate frame is allowed only if it leaves the letters, numbers and tabs uncovered. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec03-F11 | anchor: A43
Washington requires liability insurance and proof of it carried with you or kept in the vehicle. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec03-F12 | anchor: A43
Required liability coverage is at least $25,000 for injury or death of one person, at least $50,000 for injury or death of two or more people in one collision, and at least $10,000 for damage to other people's property in one collision. [A43]
Why it matters: the three limits are a frequent test item and are easy to scramble.
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec03-F13 | anchor: A44
Vehicles differ in size, engine, safety devices, technology and handling, so read the owner's manual for every vehicle you drive and learn its controls and gauges before driving. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec03-F14 | anchor: A44
Each time you get in a vehicle, adjust the steering wheel, seat and mirrors for good visibility so you can reach the pedals and instruments easily. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec03-F15 | anchor: A45
Vehicle Safety Technology (VST) and Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) support good driving habits but never replace them, and the driver stays fully responsible for the vehicle. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec03-F16 | anchor: A45
Driver-assist systems have limits: a blind-spot alert may miss a car two lanes over that is also merging, sensors may not notice people walking, rolling or riding nearby, and dirty sensors or faded markings can stop them working. [A45]
Why it matters: you must still yield as state law requires even when no alert sounds.
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec03-F17 | anchor: A45
Keep safety features switched on unless weather is so severe that their alerts become a distraction. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec03-F18 | anchor: A46
Collision avoidance features such as automatic emergency braking, forward collision warning and lane departure warning detect obstacles and warn you, while adaptive cruise control holds a set speed but slows to keep a safe gap behind the vehicle ahead. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec03-F19 | anchor: A46
Lane keeping assistance steers or alerts when you drift from your lane, blind spot detection warns of a vehicle in the next lane, and cross traffic alert warns of traffic approaching from the side, for example when backing out of a parking space. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec03-F20 | anchor: A47
Automatic high beam control adjusts headlight brightness for oncoming traffic, and collision mitigation systems such as pre-crash seat belt tensioning and post-collision braking reduce harm when a crash cannot be avoided. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec03-F21 | anchor: A47
Keeping your vehicle safe to drive is your responsibility, so heed warning lights and follow the owner's manual for routine maintenance before a small problem grows. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec03-F22 | anchor: A48
Tire tread should never be less than 2/32 of an inch, because worn tires slip and slide, especially on wet roads. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec03-F23 | anchor: A48
Low tire pressure affects handling, and the correct pressure is listed on the Tire and Loading Information label on the driver's door edge or in the owner's manual. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec03-F24 | anchor: A48
Keep glass clean inside and out, keep washer fluid full, clear all snow, ice and frost from every window before driving, and avoid hanging items or decals that block your view. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec03-F25 | anchor: A49
Washington law requires headlights from a half hour after sunset until a half hour before sunrise, and the guide suggests also using them all the time, in the dark, and in rain, snow, fog or smoke. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec03-F26 | anchor: A49
Daytime running lights are dimmer than headlights and do not turn on your taillights, so they are not a substitute for headlights. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec03-F27 | anchor: A49
If you must slow or stop where the driver behind may not expect it, tap the brake pedal three or four times quickly to warn them. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec03-F28 | anchor: A50
High beams may be used on open roads without streetlights, but dim them within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle and within 300 feet of a vehicle you are following. [A50]
Why it matters: the larger distance belongs to oncoming traffic, a classic swap on the exam.
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec03-F29 | anchor: A50
Your red brake lights must be easy to see from a distance of 100 feet, warning the driver behind you to slow and prepare to stop. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec03-F30 | anchor: A50
Always signal before changing direction, even with nobody around, start signaling 100 feet before you move, and make sure the signal stops blinking after the turn. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec03-F31 | anchor: A51
Hand signals use the left arm out the driver's window: pointing down means stop or slow, pointing straight out means a left turn, and bent upward with fingers to the sky means a right turn. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec03-F32 | anchor: A51
Turn on the flashing hazard lights when the car malfunctions or you must make an emergency stop, so others can pass you safely. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec03-F33 | anchor: A51
Sit upright with your chest at least 10 inches from the steering wheel to leave room for the airbag, hold the wheel with a gentle elbow bend, and set the headrest level with your ears to guard against whiplash. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0051]

Glossary: title — the Certificate of Ownership naming a vehicle's owners [A41]. VIN — the Vehicle Identification Number [A41]. Tabs — the yearly registration renewal [A42]. ADAS — Advanced Driver Assistance Systems that warn or assist but never drive for you [A45].
Memory aid for insurance: think of the three limits in order as one person, two or more people, then property, with property the smallest amount [A43].
